title: data-labeling-guidelines-scratchpad-lex
content:
Purpose:
- Working draft of labeler-facing guidelines and edge-case notes for the data-cleanup task (intent classification + entity spans). Mostly a scratchpad for examples and unresolved decisions.

Scope:
- Small internal dataset (12k examples) we need to clean before evals. Focus: intent label and span normalization (product_name, model_version, PII).
- This doc captures recurring annotator questions and proposed heuristics.

Quick rules (current working set):
1) Intent priority: system > user_action > recommendation > neutral. If utterance contains an explicit system command (e.g., "please restart the service", "run backup now"), mark as system even if user phrasing present.
2) Product name spans: capture canonical product only (redwood-inference -> "Redwood Inference"). If user reference is fuzzy ("redwood", "redwood.ai"), label span to the minimal token and add normalization in metadata (normalization not in this dataset; we will maintain mapping).
3) Model version tokens: detect patterns like v1, v2.0, 2024-11, llama2-13b -> label full token. If multiple versions present, prefer the one explicitly tied to the action ("upgrade to v2").
4) PII (emails, phone numbers): mark spans and also tag intent as "contains_pii" when PII is actionable (e.g., "email this to bob@example.com").

Edge cases and notes:
- Partial references to product + model: "redwood inference v2" -> two spans (product, model_version). Ensure spans are non-overlapping but adjacent.
- Hyphenated tokens: "llama-2" vs "llama2" -> treat as single token span.
- Quoted examples: when user includes code or config snippets, label only the human-language part unless the snippet is explicitly being referenced ("see config: model=llama-2").
- Non-English tokens: if majority English but contains a foreign-language product mention, annotate span but mark as "lang:other" in downstream metadata (we won't include that field here, just flag the ambiguity in comments).

Ambiguous examples (for discussion):
1) "Can you check if the redwood model failed?" -> intent: user_action? question? Proposed: label as "user_action" (diagnostic request) and add tag "ambiguous_question" for sampling.
2) "Please delete prior logs from 2024-11-01" -> is this a data-retention request (policy) or system operation? Proposed: label "system" if phrasing is imperative, else user_action.
3) "Contact support at support@redwood.ai to reset?" -> Contains PII (email) but also instruction to contact support. Label spans for email; intent "user_action" (request).

Labeler guidelines (practical):
- When unsure, leave a short note in the comment field (one-liner) describing the ambiguity. We will sample those comments in weekly review.
- Prefer minimal spans: annotate the smallest contiguous token sequence that matches the entity. Avoid including surrounding punctuation unless part of token.
- Use lowercase normalized labels for intent (system, user_action, recommendation, neutral).
- For multi-intent utterances, choose primary intent and mark secondary in comments.

Sampling and QA plan:
- Create a weekly batch of 250 examples: 200 random, 50 flagged (ambiguous/comments/previous disagreement).
- Run adjudication on flagged set with Asha + Ryan + one rotating engineer.
- Track inter-annotator agreement (Cohen's kappa) per-label and prioritize labels with kappa < 0.7 for guideline updates.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want an explicit "policy_request" intent for anything touching data deletion/compliance? (see JIRA DL-457)
- Decide on normalization field: for now, just span + comment. Later we might add normalized_text column.
- Automation: can we auto-suggest product spans using the product name list (PR #78)? Ryan to test fuzzy matching threshold.
- Create a short onboarding doc (1 page) for new labelers: examples + counterexamples. Lexi to draft.

Examples (positive / negative):
- EX1: "Restart the redwood-inference service now" -> intent: system, spans: "redwood-inference service" (product). Comment: obvious imperative.
- EX2: "How do I upgrade to v2?" -> intent: user_action, spans: "v2" (model_version).
- EX3: "I think redwood is buggy" -> intent: recommendation? neutral? Proposed: neutral (opinion) unless contains actionable request.
- EX4: "Share logs with dev@company.com" -> intent: user_action, spans: "dev@company.com" (PII).

Quick links & refs:
- Confluence: Data Labeling Playbook (link above).
- JIRA: DL-457 (policy request taxonomy)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/data-labeling/pull/78 (product fuzzy match)

Notes from labeler feedback (last week):
- Several labelers asked for a clear rule on "imperative vs. question" phrasing. Suggest adding a short decision tree: does the sentence contain a direct verb command? If yes -> system. Otherwise -> user_action/question. Still ambiguous for polite requests ("could you please restart?") -> treat as user_action.
- Labelers also asked for a canonical product list. Engineering to provide the updated list (product-registry.csv) and expose via S3.

Next steps (my TODO):
- Draft the 1-page onboarding and upload to Confluence (by 2026-03-10).
- Run a quick fuzzy-match test with PR #78 and report precision/recall on 500 labeled examples (Ryan).
- Collate flagged comments into a short doc for the adjudication meeting (weekly).

-- Lexi
